summary: Background Automation: Scheduled Session Transitions & Cross-Entity Status Cascade
description:
Replaces the background-job story in docs/backlog/phase-3-epic-weeks-7-8-feedback-job-search.json with a scope that matches the actual codebase: a single-module Spring Boot backend (backend/api, package xyz.catuns.imp.api) with an already-built session status state machine and Kafka producer, but no scheduler and no cross-entity cascade logic yet. Drops the advisory-lock/Micrometer/separate-service framing from the original spec — there is no evidence of a multi-instance deployment, and SessionStatusTransitionService.transitionByJob(...) already exists as a ready-made entry point (ChangeSource.BACKGROUND_JOB) that nothing currently calls.

Product decision: process status becomes fully derived from session outcomes, so a marketer's only manual actions are (a) mark a session PASSED, (b) mark a session REJECTED, or (c) schedule a new session — everything else follows automatically. The one manual-only escape hatch is CANCELLED: once a process is cancelled (independent business decision, e.g. client pulled the role), no session-driven cascade overwrites it; only an explicit PATCH /processes/:id can move it out of CANCELLED.

Four system-initiated behaviors are in scope:
1. Time-based: SCHEDULED sessions past their scheduledAt auto-transition to IN_REVIEW on an hourly job.
2. Session→process cascade: a session transitioning to REJECTED auto-transitions its parent process to WITHDRAWN.
3. Session→process cascade: a session transitioning to PASSED auto-transitions its parent process to COMPLETED.
4. Session→session and session→process cascade: scheduling a new session for a process (a) auto-transitions any of that process's sessions still in IN_REVIEW to PASSED (which itself triggers behavior 3), then (b) reactivates the process to ACTIVE and clears closedAt — so adding the next round always wins over whatever terminal state the prior round just produced.

Key paths: <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/job> (new), <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/session/SessionStatusTransitionService.java>, <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/session/InterviewSessionService.java>, <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/process/InterviewProcessService.java>
functionality: automatically keep process status in sync with session outcomes, so a marketer only ever marks a session PASSED/REJECTED or schedules the next round — never manually patches process status for the normal lifecycle
benefit: removes manual status-management overhead and eliminates the stale/inconsistent process statuses that happen when marketers forget to update a process after a session outcome is recorded

stories.summary: Implement hourly scheduled job to auto-transition overdue SCHEDULED sessions to IN_REVIEW
stories.description:
Add a @Scheduled job that runs hourly, finds sessions with status=SCHEDULED and scheduledAt in the past, and transitions each to IN_REVIEW via the existing SessionStatusTransitionService.transitionByJob(...) method. Since status_history.changed_by is nullable, background-initiated transitions pass null rather than requiring a synthetic 'system user' row.

Key paths: <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/job/SessionAutoTransitionJob.java> (new), <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/session/repository/InterviewSessionRepository.java>

stories.summary: Cascade terminal session outcomes to process status (PASSED→COMPLETED, REJECTED→WITHDRAWN)
stories.description:
When a session transitions to PASSED or REJECTED — whether via the manual PATCH /sessions/:id/status endpoint or a background-initiated transition — automatically update the parent InterviewProcess status (COMPLETED for PASSED, WITHDRAWN for REJECTED) and set closedAt to now. CANCELLED is the one process state this cascade never overwrites: if the process is already CANCELLED, the cascade is a no-op, since cancellation is an independent manual decision. Any other current process status (ACTIVE, COMPLETED, WITHDRAWN) is overwritten to reflect the latest session outcome — this lets a later round's REJECTED withdraw a process that a prior round had already marked COMPLETED, matching the fully-derived status model. NO_SHOW and CANCELLED session statuses do not cascade to the process in this story.

Key paths: <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/session/SessionStatusTransitionService.java>, <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/process/repository/InterviewProcessRepository.java>

acceptanceCriteria.given: a session belongs to a process with status ACTIVE
acceptanceCriteria.when: the session transitions from IN_REVIEW to REJECTED
acceptanceCriteria.then: the process status is updated to WITHDRAWN, closedAt is set to the current time, in the same transaction as the session transition

acceptanceCriteria.given: a session belongs to a process with status ACTIVE
acceptanceCriteria.when: the session transitions from IN_REVIEW to PASSED
acceptanceCriteria.then: the process status is updated to COMPLETED and closedAt is set to the current time

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: A later outcome overwrites an earlier one

acceptanceCriteria.when: a subsequent round's session on the same process transitions to REJECTED
acceptanceCriteria.then: the process status is overwritten to WITHDRAWN and closedAt is updated to the new time

acceptanceCriteria.then: the process status and closedAt remain unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.given: a session belongs to an ACTIVE process
acceptanceCriteria.when: the session transitions to NO_SHOW or CANCELLED

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Cascade applies regardless of transition source
acceptanceCriteria.given: a session is transitioned to PASSED or REJECTED by the background job rather than a manual PATCH
acceptanceCriteria.then: the same process cascade runs, unaffected by change_source

stories.summary: Cascade new session creation to auto-pass the prior IN_REVIEW session and reactivate the process
stories.description:
When a marketer or admin schedules a new session for a process (POST /processes/:id/sessions), two things happen in order, in the same transaction: (1) any existing session on that process still in IN_REVIEW status is transitioned to PASSED via SessionStatusTransitionService.transitionByJob(...) — which, per the previous story, will itself set the process to COMPLETED; then (2) the process is reactivated to ACTIVE with closedAt cleared to null, since scheduling the next round means the process is ongoing again. Order matters: step 2 always runs after step 1, so the net effect of adding a new round to a just-completed process is that the prior session ends up PASSED and the process ends up ACTIVE, not COMPLETED. As with the other cascades, a process in CANCELLED status is left untouched — a cancelled process cannot be silently reactivated by scheduling a session against it.

Key paths: <backend/api/src/main/java/xyz/catuns/imp/api/session/InterviewSessionService.java>

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Prior IN_REVIEW session is auto-passed when the next round is scheduled
acceptanceCriteria.given: a process has a session in IN_REVIEW status
acceptanceCriteria.when: a marketer calls POST /processes/:id/sessions to schedule a new session on the same process
acceptanceCriteria.then: the IN_REVIEW session is transitioned to PASSED with a status_history row (change_source=BACKGROUND_JOB), and the new session is created with status SCHEDULED

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Process ends up ACTIVE, not COMPLETED, after adding the next round
acceptanceCriteria.given: a process has a session in IN_REVIEW status
acceptanceCriteria.when: a new session is scheduled for that process, triggering the prior session's PASSED cascade to COMPLETED
acceptanceCriteria.then: the process's final status after the request completes is ACTIVE with closedAt=null, not COMPLETED

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Reactivation applies even to an already-COMPLETED or WITHDRAWN process
acceptanceCriteria.given: a process has status COMPLETED or WITHDRAWN from a previous round's outcome
acceptanceCriteria.when: a marketer schedules a new session for that process
acceptanceCriteria.then: the process status is set to ACTIVE and closedAt is cleared

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: CANCELLED processes are not reactivated by session creation
acceptanceCriteria.when: a new session is scheduled for that process
acceptanceCriteria.then: the session is still created, but the process status remains CANCELLED

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: No side effect when nothing is in review
acceptanceCriteria.given: a process has no sessions in IN_REVIEW status
acceptanceCriteria.when: a new session is created for that process
acceptanceCriteria.then: no other session's status changes, and the process is still reactivated to ACTIVE per the rules above

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Multiple IN_REVIEW sessions are all auto-passed
acceptanceCriteria.given: a process has two sessions concurrently in IN_REVIEW status (an edge case)
acceptanceCriteria.when: a new session is created for that process
acceptanceCriteria.then: both IN_REVIEW sessions transition to PASSED
